title: Scam alert, read as news
hook: A consumer-finance story — a rewards scheme and a denied claim — staged as a breaking-news bulletin. Virtual set, ticker, lower thirds and a cold open that buys the next sixty seconds.

title: Four debits he never approved
hook: Bank SMS cards stack up over a desk reaction until the autopay list lays all four out on one screen.

title: Old method vs smart method
hook: A straight compare: the bank queue on one side, chai and a phone on the other, with the supers doing the arguing.

title: Every payment, out loud
hook: Street-side direct address cut into the autopay list, then the voice-alert end card. Built around one presenter and one phone.

title: What McDonald's actually sells
hook: Presenter-led business explainer cut against b-roll, charts and brand cut-outs, paced to hold past the first three seconds.

title: The register that never adds up
hook: An hour lost to a paper attendance book, answered by the report screen that closes the month in a tap.

title: Two banks, one screen
hook: Two men over one phone in a kirana store. The passbook screen does the talking and the voice-alert pitch lands on the last beat.

title: Learn in six languages
hook: A UPI receipt, a street vendor and a presenter walking the viewer to the subscription card. Cut for the ffreedom app, since renamed Boss Wallah.

title: Due tomorrow, dismissed today
hook: Shop-floor dialogue into the upcoming-payments screen, with the dismiss-or-pay beat held long enough to actually read.

title: Rush hour at the general store
hook: A counter full of customers and a man who cannot tell which payment landed. Cut tight to keep the pressure on until the app arrives.
